raw_recipe.headline: Fry Sauce
raw_recipe.description: A simple French fry dipping sauce made by blending tangy ketchup with creamy mayonnaise. This also tastes great on onion rings and fried clams!
raw_recipe.name: Fry Sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Mix ketchup and mayonnaise together in a small bowl until thoroughly blended.

review.reviewBody: My mother worked at a Ogden, UT Blue Onion restaurant in the early 70's, so we grew up with this. It is a very simple and general condiment for lots of things in place of ketchup, mayo or similar condiments. I have always known and made it as the "Secret Sauce" because that's what mom called it. None of our friends knew about it when we moved to CA or elsewhere. We've converted a lot of people that just can't do plain ketchup any more. You can tweak the ratio to whatever your preference is...(more mayo, more ketchup or 50/50). You really can't mess it up. We've never measured it. It's great to see someone put this recipe up to share---why didn't I think of it! LOL

Ketchup and Mayo alone is not Utah fry sauce. 
2 parts mayo to 1 part ketchup and white vinegar.
1/8 c mayo, 1 1/2 T ketchup, 1/2t white vinegar. 
(The white vinegar makes it smooth and adds flavor)
Thats the recipe! :-)

I think it's funny that a lot of people aren't familiar with fry sauce! It comes with everything here (in Oregon). I didn't know the proportions to make it, so I looked up this recipe. However, I followed the advice of other reviewers and did about 50% mayo, 40% ketchup, and 10% barbeque (Big Al's KC Barbeque from this site). Mmm, mmm, mmm! Very good.

I couldn’t figure out what the salad dressing ingredient could be so In addition to the mayo and ketchup I added 1/2 tsp. smoked paprika, 1 tbsp worcestershire sauce, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp sugar. It is great on everything, fries, hamburgers, chicken. We love it.

It was the Artic Circle in Midvale, Utah that created this delicious little wonder & during my 10 year stint there, I drank this sauce like it was mothers milk. We even made salad dressing out of it. Here's my advice. Go 50/50 on the mayo to ketchup ratio. Mix & taste, then figure out which you prefer more of & go from there in a larger batch. Usually its more mayonnaise than ketchup. You CAN also add a drop of liquid smoke & have it taste exactly like major restaurant chains but that's NOT what REAL Utah Fry Sauce is about. If it ain't broke folks......Sometimes simplicity is its own perfection.

The recipe I used is slightly different but basically the same. My recipe uses 1/4 cup barbecue sauce and 1 cup of mayonnaise. This is the very best dipping sauce ever. I rarely use ketchup for fries but I,ll use this sauce. Even my grandchildren like this.

Born and raised Utahn. More ketchup, less mayo, that much mayo is just too rich. Some like a splash of dill or sweet pickle juice, or even a drop of liquid smoke. Some will add a dash of Lawreys Seasoned Salt. Just mayo and ketchup is great though. McDonald's in Utah will often give you a tablespoon or two of mayo in a box if you want to make your own. I've seen it plenty of other places on the shelfs labeled mayotchup or some blend of the words.

I have never tried traditional fry sauce but created my own version when I was 8 and have eaten it ever since on almost everything. I mix 3 parts mayo (preferably Miracle Whip but never Hellman's) to 2 parts ketchup, to 1 part yellow mustard. Give or take on the ratios depending on if my Crohn's Disease is acting up I'll cut the mustard in half. I always mix my own rather than buy the pre-made bottled stuff. That way I can control the spiciness of it.

My Niece, who owns a couple of restaurants uses "Fry Sauce" with fresh snipped or dried Dill Weed mixed in, on her Reuben Sandwiches, in place of "regular" 1000 Island Dressing ...

Myself, I sieve a hard boiled egg and a splash of lemon juice mixed with the "Dill Fry Sauce" and use for a shrimp cocktail sauce ... 
It's pretty tasty as a bread spread for plain old cheese sandwiches also ...

Try adding 1/2 tsp of white vinegar to it!!! I also use onion and garlic powder in mine. Those 3 things give it so much flavor! I use to not use anything for fries until I came across this recipe. I can't get enough of it!!! If you want some kick to it add some cayenne powder! Yum!!!
Great base recipe. I like to add a tablespoon or 2 of BBQ sauce and a dash of hot sauce to really make this an AMAZING fry sauce.

I am a native Utahn, and we have used this for as long as I can remember. There is a local fast food chain that "claims" they invented this (Arctic Circle). The 50/50 ketchup and mayo mix is a good base recipe. Tweak however you like. onion powder, garlic powder, paprika, liquid smoke, sweet pickle relish, BBQ sauce. Pick your poison.
The way my dad made it was to also add some finely diced onion.

Not for nothing but this is nothing new and an East Coast creation. This is called mayo-ketchup which has vinegar and we have been eating this since I was a kid. I am 61. We also add garlic to it for our fried tostones. 🙂
So good! I added a touch of liquid smoke to it lime one of the suggestions. Good call! Delicious!

This was a great recipe. I did change the ratio a bit. I went with 1/2 & 1/2 with the mayo and ketchup. 
My family loved it. I grilled burgers and made some fries and they were dipping the burgers as well as the fries. They want the sauce whenever I do burgers and fries.
I have had this many times. Try it on french fried shrimp. That's where I first learned to love it.
the recipe should read: two parts mayonnaise, one part ketchup, one part white vinegar.
I always make it with vinegar to taste because we like a bit of zing to it. We have it with fries but it also goes great with chicken nuggets.
Good sauce though and many good comments to spice it up! I'll be trying a few more versions...time to get some frings ready!
